For a first printed enclosure, I would consider PETG for a tougher, somewhat more heat-tolerant housing than ordinary PLA; PLA is easier for an initial fit prototype. A screw-fastened lid is durable and serviceable, while a snap lid avoids hardware but needs printer-specific fit trials. These are recommendations, not settled dimensions or material performance guarantees. Use millimetres throughout. This is a modeling plan for the synthetic specification; no CAD has been created.

Parameters: board 80 × 50 × 12; side gap 2; standoff height 3; headroom 5; wall/base/lid 2. Internal cavity = 84 × 54 × 20 (3 + 12 + 5 high). Body exterior excluding lid = 88 × 58 × 22; lid = 88 × 58 × 2; assembled exterior = 88 × 58 × 24. Datum: external lower-left-bottom, x along 88, y along 58, z upward. Board lower-left-bottom = (4,4,5). Its hole axes are at external XY (7,7), (81,7), (81,51), (7,51).

Feature order:
1. Base part: Top-plane rectangle 88 × 58, constrained at the datum; extrude 22.
2. On its upper face sketch a centered 84 × 54 rectangle with 2 mm offsets and cut 20 deep, leaving the 2 mm floor.
3. Four Ø6 bosses on the internal floor at the hole-axis XY coordinates; extrude 3 to z=5. Create a blind Ø2.5 pilot in each top, depth 2, ending at z=3.
4. Right external x-face: Ø6 opening centered at y=29,z=12; cut through the 2 mm wall only, checking the cut direction. The right external face is x=88.
5. Separate lid part: 88 × 58 rectangle extruded 2. No lid screws or vents. External straps provide retention; keep strap geometry outside the enclosure until separately specified.
6. Assembly: position lid underside at z=22, constrained to body orientation and alignment. Retain the lift-off behavior in the design intent; use assembly configurations or suppress the retention mate when demonstrating removal.

Checks: dimensions above, floor/wall/lid thickness, 4 boss axes and pilot depths, 2 mm board side clearances, 5 mm headroom, cable-opening location and unobstructed cable route, and a clean rebuild. Check Ø3.2 board-hole clearance over the pilots using the selected hardware; the Ø6 bosses support the board rather than pass through those holes. Inspect all features in section. PETG FDM, open side up: check supports/bridging at the cable opening and print a pilot/fastener coupon. Physical fit and screw engagement remain unverified. Native parts/assembly and exports are later construction deliverables, not outputs of this plan-only request.

Use a user-run VBA macro: your Mac and the separate Windows PC have no verified live connection. The following is source text, not a runnable .swp project or an existing CAD model. It creates a fresh 80 × 40 × 3 mm part on each run and refuses an existing output filename.

On Windows in SOLIDWORKS 2024, confirm a default part template under Tools → Options → Default Templates. Choose Tools → Macro → New, save a new VBA .swp project, and replace the generated module code with the source below. Alternatively save the source as Plate.bas and import it using File → Import File in the VBA editor, removing the unused generated module so there is only one main entry point. Check Tools → References for the installed SOLIDWORKS type/constant libraries and any MISSING entry. Save the project; transfer source files manually to a Windows folder you choose. Renaming a text file .swp does not create a macro project.

```vb
Option Explicit

Sub main()
    Dim app As SldWorks.SldWorks
    Dim model As SldWorks.ModelDoc2
    Dim plane As SldWorks.Feature, boss As SldWorks.Feature
    Dim segments As Variant
    Dim outPath As String, stage As String
    Dim errors As Long, warnings As Long
    Dim ok As Boolean
    On Error GoTo Failed

    stage = "output path"
    outPath = InputBox("New full Windows path ending in .sldprt; existing files are refused")
    If Len(outPath) = 0 Then Exit Sub
    If LCase$(Right$(outPath, 7)) <> ".sldprt" Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 1, , "Use a .sldprt filename"
    If Len(Dir$(outPath)) > 0 Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 2, , "Output already exists; choose a fresh filename"

    Set app = Application.SldWorks
    stage = "new part (default template)"
    Set model = app.NewPart
    If model Is Nothing Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 3, , "No new part; configure the default part template"

    stage = "reference plane"
    Set plane = model.FirstFeature
    Do While Not plane Is Nothing
        If plane.GetTypeName2 = "RefPlane" Then Exit Do
        Set plane = plane.GetNextFeature
    Loop
    If plane Is Nothing Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 4, , "No reference plane in template"
    If Not plane.Select2(False, 0) Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 5, , "Plane selection failed"
    model.SketchManager.InsertSketch True
    stage = "rectangle, native API meters"
    segments = model.SketchManager.CreateCornerRectangle(0, 0, 0, 80# / 1000#, 40# / 1000#, 0)
    If IsEmpty(segments) Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 6, , "Rectangle was not returned"
    model.SketchManager.InsertSketch True

    stage = "extrusion, 3 mm = 0.003 m"
    Set boss = model.FeatureManager.FeatureExtrusion2(True, False, False, 0, 0, 3# / 1000#, 0#, False, False, False, False, 0#, 0#, False, False, False, False, True, True, True, 0, 0#, False)
    If boss Is Nothing Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 7, , "No extrusion feature returned"
    stage = "rebuild"
    If Not model.ForceRebuild3(False) Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 8, , "Rebuild failed"

    stage = "save"
    model.ClearSelection2 True
    If Len(Dir$(outPath)) > 0 Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 9, , "Output appeared during construction; refusing overwrite"
    ok = model.Extension.SaveAs(outPath, 0, 1, Nothing, errors, warnings)
    If Not ok Or errors <> 0 Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 10, , "Save failed; errors=" & CStr(errors) & "; warnings=" & CStr(warnings)
    If Len(Dir$(outPath)) = 0 Then Err.Raise vbObjectError + 11, , "Save reported success but file not found"
    MsgBox "Saved " & outPath & vbCrLf & "Warnings=" & CStr(warnings) & vbCrLf & "Inspect dimensions/features before accepting.", vbInformation
    Exit Sub
Failed:
    MsgBox "Stopped at " & stage & ": " & Err.Description & vbCrLf & "Existing documents were not closed. Inspect the new part before rerunning.", vbExclamation
End Sub
```

1. Create a new Part. Select the standard plane on which you want the broad 60 × 30 face; Front is convenient. If your interface is localized, choose that plane by its orientation rather than relying on the English name. Start a sketch.
2. Draw a center rectangle centered on the sketch origin. Add a horizontal width of 60 mm and vertical height of 30 mm. Keep its horizontal/vertical relations and center coincident with the origin. Expected result: a fully constrained rectangle, 30 mm left/right and 15 mm above/below the center.
3. Exit the sketch. Use Extruded Boss/Base with a blind depth of 4 mm. Confirm the preview produces a solid rectangular plate and accept.
4. Rebuild and use Measure to check 60 × 30 × 4 mm. The tree should contain the sketch and one boss extrusion with no feature errors. Save as a new .sldprt filename. Stop after this stage if any dimension, constraint or preview differs; no macro is needed.

With the exterior fixed at 100 × 70 mm, 3 mm side walls leave a 94 × 64 mm cavity: 100−2×3 and 70−2×3. The former 96 × 66 cavity shrinks by 2 mm in each direction. Your required 95 × 65 board-and-gap envelope exceeds the revised cavity by 1 mm in each direction, so the revision does not fit.

I would update the brief and wall parameter to 3 mm, retain the exterior and unchanged base/lid, and mark fit as failed. Treat this as an assembly with three editable parts: a base, hinged arm and camera clamp. I would plan a concentric hinge mate plus an angular limit for the arm, and a clamp interface that can later be adapted to the selected camera. The hinge needs a deliberate lock or friction mechanism; a freely rotating pin alone will not hold an adjusted position.

What maximum camera-plus-accessories mass should the bracket support? An approximate target is useful while the camera is undecided. That load target informs the arm section, hinge fastener and base attachment. Then we can settle camera/clamp dimensions, reach and angular travel. I would not assume a particular tripod thread or camera envelope. Assembly checks will include pivot travel, mate freedom, collisions and holding-load/physical tests; enclosure questions do not apply.

A fully defined sketch has no remaining unintended freedom: dimensions and geometric relations fix its size, shape, and position relative to the origin or other references. In the default SOLIDWORKS display its entities are normally black. It does not by itself prove the chosen dimensions or design are correct.

Draft the enclosure parametrically, leaving the actual board dimensions unresolved:

- Board envelope B_L, B_W, B_H; mounting-hole coordinates H1…Hn, all pending measurement in mm.
- Proposed first-fit clearances: side gap c, floor-to-board stand-off s, overhead gap h; choose numeric values only as provisional design choices when the board and printing method are known.
- Proposed wall/base/lid thickness t_w, t_b, t_l. Inner cavity = (B_L+2c) × (B_W+2c) × (s+B_H+h). Exterior = inner length/width plus 2t_w; total height = t_b+s+B_H+h+t_l.
- Separate base and lift-off lid; start with screws for repeatable service access if hardware is acceptable, or use straps for an early no-fastener prototype. Mark retention choice provisional.
